my 44 year old friend, did $340,000 from YouTube this year and he doesn't own a f**cking channel, no subscribers, no social media presence, nothing!!!!

yet he makes more on YouTube than niggas grinding their ass to post the next viral LONGFORM

He leaked everything to me.

and he called it the REVERSE EFFECT OF TRUMPETING.

he didn't have influencers shout out his stuff.

He did none of that.

Yet, he kept siphoning leads out of YouTube.

I'm in a good mood, so I'll leak everything.

Internet YT in 2025 is a fallacy.

whilst everyone is grinding, recording, editing, and trying to get monetized off YouTube.

There are soft niggas who never show themselves on the internet, yet they make more than those parading everyday for attention.

here's the playbook you never understood ↓

currently 90% of YT videos posted are dumbsh*t.

You have a creator desperate for winning the algorithm.

Posting 1 hour BS in the name of “VALUE”

Every single video looks great, but at the end the viewers leave unsatisfied, tired and searching for the next solution on the YT search.

people hardly watch educational YouTube videos.

what they do is this ↓

➼ Get stuck in a problem or task, probably business issue, finance platforms, selling to a client who's Skeptical, simple but critical issues.

➼ go on YouTube and search with the keyword “How to run cold emails without external assistance”

➼ Scroll for tutorials

➼ find one with a hooking title, fast forward ten seconds.

➼ take the link and get the transcript.

➼ transcript looks confusing

➼ go back to the video to watch 

➼ video too lengthy

➼ Check Comments

That's where he strikes.

someone would post a 30 minute video: “How I Built a 6-Figure Shopify Store.”

solid content. good production. 200K views.

but every comment section told the same story:

→ “great video but how do you actually find winning products?”

→ “loved this but got stuck on the Facebook ads part”

→ “anyone know a good supplier? he didn't mention that”

→ “this worked in 2021 but doesn't Meta block this now?”

the video answered the question in the title, but created 12 new questions in the viewer's head.

“creators optimize for watch time and retention. not for actually solving the problem completely. there's always a gap. that gap is where I live.”

80% of decisions on the internet are validated off comments.

In comments you find people aligning, some shitting on the video, and then my friend driving Perception.

He doesn't do it.

He has a team who does it, 250 real accounts, hired people in the Philippines, paid monthly, gave them training docs on how to spot gaps, how to comment naturally. how to validate each other without being obvious.

Each account

➼ Follows a big page and small creators rising

➼ subscribed to 400+ channels each across business, finance, health, relationships, tech tutorials.

➼ Real profile picture

➼ they'd screen for videos hitting 10K views in the first 48 hours. early signal.

➼ Big accounts post they wait for confirmation and strike

➼ Small accounts post they strike

➼ All 250 real commenters are in one group, called the perception hub.

➼ Videos are dropped every 9 hours

➼ Commenters comment separately in 10 minutes intervals per batches of 20

➼ 10% of the commenters reply to their fellow commenter to validate thoughts

➼ 100% of the commenters like their fellow Commenters comments to push the comment in ranking.

➼ 249 commenters like 1 comment post, vice versa

➼ Comments gets pushed, anyone opening the video sees the comment first.

➼ Scroll comments? You see more

➼ when the same confusion of something appeared 8+ times, they moved.

➼ created a micro-product in 12-18 hours. Notion template. video course module. spreadsheet. checklist. guide. whatever format fit.
price point: $27-$67. impulse buy range.

➼ And the perception drive is created

This is how it works ↓

the comments.

not spam. not links. just organic mentions.

“struggled with this exact thing for weeks, ended up using the Davidson Method breakdown (think it's on Gumroad?). it's the only thing that actually explained the tracking setup step by step.”

6 other accounts would interact over the next 90 minutes.

→ “what's the Davidson Method?”

→ “just grabbed it. legit actually.”

→ “okay but is it actually worth $50 or is it basic?”

→ “I mean it's $49 and it's literally the missing piece from this video so yeah”

the comments would cluster near the top. upvoted by the team. replied to by real viewers now.

“we never sell in the comment. we reference. humans trust references more than recommendations. we're not affiliates. we're not promoting. we're just people who already solved this specific problem.”

HE GOT SYSTEMATIC.

they produce 6-8 micro-products a month. some flop. most break even. 2-3 hit big.

“we made $38K in November on a cold email template pack for B2B sales. video had 380K views. guy spent 18 minutes on strategy but never showed his actual templates. comments were begging for examples. we made 7 templates in Notion. $39. sold 970 copies in 6 weeks.”

I asked the obvious question.

➼ isn't this manipulating people?

“is it manipulation when the video promised a complete solution and didn't deliver? I'm solving the actual problem. I'm just better at identifying what people need than the creator was. and I don't need my face on camera to do it.”

he said most creators are too close to their content.

“they think their video is complete because they covered what they think matters. but the audience tells you what actually matters. it's right there in the comments. most creators never read them.”

➼ no paid ads?

“never. paid ads create resistance. comments create curiosity. nobody thinks a comment is trying to sell them something.”

➼ no email list?

“I have a list now. 14,000 people. but it came from the products, not the other way around. I didn't build an audience first. I solved problems first. audience is a side effect.”

➼ no brand?

“I have 20 brands. whatever name fits the niche. Davidson Method. Chen Systems. Apex Templates. Rivera Framework. none of them are me. all of them are just signals of authority. people don't buy from people anymore. they buy from things that sound like they've already helped other people.”

➼ I asked what happens when YouTube cracks down on this.

“they won't. we're not violating TOS. we're not spamming. we're real accounts having real conversations. the Federal Trade Commission requires disclosure for affiliate links and sponsorships. we're not affiliates. we're customers recommending products. is that illegal? is word-of-mouth illegal now?”

he opened his notebook and showed me his tracking sheet.

47 active videos being monitored. 12 products in various stages. conversion rates per niche. comment engagement scores.

all handwritten!

“I don't automate this part. automation makes you stupid. I read 200 comments a day myself still. that's where the insights are. that's where the money is.”

We went out, had some steaks, and I left.

📢 STOP TO AI FANTASY!📢: YouTube’s Hard Line on Synthetic Content

YouTube is taking a definitive stand on the wave of AI-generated content flooding the platform. In a major policy shift, the focus is moving away from "AI for the sake of AI" and toward transparency, realism, and educational value.

🔍 The "Real vs. Synthetic" Threshold
YouTube now mandates that creators disclose when realistic-looking content has been created or altered using AI. This isn't just about labels; it’s about trust. If a video looks real but is synthetic, the audience has a right to know.

🎓 Educational Value is the New Gold Standard
The platform is tightening its grip on "low-effort" AI fantasy content. Moving forward, AI-generated material that deals with sensitive topics will be judged through the EDSA lens:

- Educational

- Documentary

- Scientific

- Artistic

Purely "imaginary" AI content that mimics reality without providing tangible educational utility or a clear artistic purpose faces stricter scrutiny, reduced reach, or removal.

🛡️ Why This Matters
This decision marks a turning point in the battle against misinformation. By prioritizing content that teaches, informs, or documents—rather than just simulates—YouTube is ensuring that the next generation of digital media remains a tool for learning, not just a hall of mirrors.

"Innovation must be balanced with responsibility. We are prioritizing AI that adds value to the human experience, not content that replaces truth with fiction."

WHAT DO YOU THINK?👇

#YouTubeUpdate #ArtificialIntelligence #ContentCreators #DigitalEthics #TechNews2025
